abstract: Maintains oceanographic moonpool operational readiness and underwater acoustic interference surveys
system_message:
You are Marine science instrumentation lead (INST). The Marine science instrumentation lead (INST) maintains records on oceanographic moonpool operational readiness and underwater acoustic interference surveys, as well as deck machinery capacities including oceanographic winch specifications.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains oceanographic moonpool operational readiness and underwater acoustic interference surveys（ACOUST）
information_points.content:
INST-ACOUST-WEZ：For the Aurora Australis Explorer, verified mechanical seal operation and opening clearance confirm that onboard moonpool deployment readiness is true for the internal sea-level instrument deployment moonpool. Acoustic signature surveys of the primary multi-beam hydrographic transducer array at 8 knots record an acoustic baseline interference level of 42 dB mean background noise across the 12 to 38 kHz band.
INST-ACOUST-804：For the Nordic Sentinel Multi-Purpose Vessel, verified mechanical seal operation and opening clearance confirm that onboard moonpool deployment readiness is true for the internal sea-level instrument deployment moonpool. Acoustic signature surveys of the primary multi-beam hydrographic transducer array at 8 knots record an acoustic baseline interference level of 56 dB mean background noise across the 12 to 38 kHz band.
INST-ACOUST-NIS：For the Polaris Endurance Icebreaker, verified mechanical seal operation and opening clearance confirm that onboard moonpool deployment readiness is true for the internal sea-level instrument deployment moonpool. Acoustic signature surveys of the primary multi-beam hydrographic transducer array at 8 knots record an acoustic baseline interference level of 42 dB mean background noise across the 12 to 38 kHz band.

information_points.title: Oceanographic winch capacity（WINCH）
information_points.content:
INST-WINCH-TUH：Deck machinery inspections for the Aurora Australis Explorer show the aft hydrographic traction winch carries a continuous spoolable synthetic deep-tow winch cable length of 8,000 m.
INST-WINCH-5PF：Deck machinery inspections for the Polaris Endurance Icebreaker show the aft hydrographic traction winch carries a continuous spoolable synthetic deep-tow winch cable length of 6,000 m.
INST-WINCH-0Q2：Deck machinery inspections for the Nordic Sentinel Multi-Purpose Vessel show the aft hydrographic traction winch carries a continuous spoolable synthetic deep-tow winch cable length of 4,000 m.
